lessons: cycles 1-7 (retrospective, added with the strategy upgrade): The CAT round-trip validated evidence-based decisions both ways - cycle 5 correctly held CAT through a -5% dip when research showed strength (dividend raise, target hikes), and cycle 7 correctly exited when research showed real deterioration (margin compression, tariff guide, downgrade). The differentiator was actual research, not the price move itself.

cycles 1-7 (retrospective): Buys were made without pre-committed invalidation triggers or next-earnings dates; two weekend cycles (4, 6) couldn't trade. cycle 8: Holding NVDA/GOOGL/AMZN through the Cycle 6-7 AI-capex-jitters sell-off (research-based, not reflexive) was vindicated — AMZN's AWS-driven Q2 beat produced a same-day +14.7% pop, and GOOGL rallied +3% on AI optimism plus its own Cloud-profitability beat. Lesson reinforced: a name that beats and executes doesn't get trimmed just because the sector re-rated down first.

cycle 8: LIN dropped -9.4% from cost despite *beating* Q2 estimates — the move was pure guidance-vs-consensus multiple compression (Q3 guide $4.45-4.55 vs $4.59 consensus), not a broken business (margins and sales growth both still healthy). Distinguishing 'guidance landed a hair below consensus on a premium multiple' from 'the business is actually deteriorating' is exactly the kind of judgment call this process exists to make well.

cycle 9: MSFT/AMZN/GOOGL continued rallying into Friday's close (MSFT +20.4% from cost, AMZN +10.6%) after the Cycle 8 mid-session beat check — a real earnings beat tends to keep compounding through the session and beyond, reinforcing that holding through the print (not trimming into strength out of nervousness) was the right call.

cycle 10: CAT beat Q2 estimates by 32% (EPS $8.17 vs $6.17) with op margin +360bps and a record $72B backlog — the Cycle 7 exit thesis (tariff/margin compression) reversed faster than expected. Lesson: a cyclical's margin narrative can flip in one quarter given a real demand catalyst (here, AI data-center capex), but a same-day +5-11% earnings pop is still a chase, not an entry — wait for the move to settle before acting on a reversed thesis.

cycle 10: LIN's fundamentals stayed healthy (record backlog, analyst PT raised post-dip) but the stock is in a confirmed technical downtrend (price ~6% below its 50-day SMA, RSI 31) — a reminder that 'the business is fine' and 'the chart says wait' can both be true at once; STRATEGY.md's scoring rubric (trend scored 1/5, disqualifying) did its job by blocking an add into a falling knife despite good fundamentals.

cycle 11: CAT's post-earnings spike (Cycle 10) fully round-tripped — price fell from the same-day high back below its 50-day SMA within 3 trading days (PE still ~41x). Confirms the execution rule against chasing >5% intraday pops: even a real fundamental reversal needs the move to consolidate, not just fade, before it's a legitimate technical entry.
